explanation: Basque, or its direct ancestor, was spoken in the region before the Romans brought Latin, the ancestor of Spanish and French. No proposed link to another family has won general acceptance.

claims.text: Basque is a language isolate: no relationship between Basque and any other language family has been proven.
Basque or its direct ancestor was spoken in the region before Latin arrived with the Romans.
Spanish and French descend from Latin.
Proposed links between Basque and other language families have not been generally accepted.

writerNotes: Most players assume a European language must be related to its neighbours, so they say false; counterintuitive is true. The key is a claim about every other language family, a superlative in disguise, so it is high with that reason (the schema has no counterintuitive reason). Self-check (9.3): lint run clean; every claim listed with risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where honest; datasets: cldr-languages lists eu as Basque by name only; no dataset covers language families; rival test: argued for Aquitanian as a relative: it is usually treated as an ancient form of Basque itself, not a separate relative, so the isolate claim stands; volatility evergreen, no time words, nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026; regional: a fact about Europe that no country's schooling owns; style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes, explanation within 35 words; myths: no match in myths.json; mystery and encore checks: not applicable to a practice item; doubts: none
